title: Early Humans and River Valley Civilizations
subject: Social Studies

questions.question: Which development marks the beginning of the Neolithic Revolution?
choices: The shift toward farming and settled communities
The creation of the first written constitutions

questions.question: Why did agriculture support the growth of permanent settlements?
choices: Farming eliminated the need for water
Food production could create surpluses that supported larger communities
Crops could grow without labor or land

questions.question: Which river system supported early Mesopotamian civilizations?
Why were many early civilizations located near rivers?
choices: Rivers provided water, fertile soils, transportation, and other resources
Rivers prevented floods in every season
River valleys were isolated from trade

questions.question: What was cuneiform?
choices: A writing system developed in Mesopotamia

questions.question: How did irrigation help early farmers in dry regions?
choices: It removed the need to plant crops
It carried water to fields when rainfall was insufficient

questions.question: Which ancient civilization developed along the Nile River in northeastern Africa?
A settlement's food supply becomes more reliable, and some residents specialize as craftspeople or officials. What does this suggest?
choices: Agricultural surplus can support occupational specialization
Trade must end when farming expands
Every resident must produce the same goods

questions.question: Which feature is most associated with the Indus Valley cities of Harappa and Mohenjo-daro?
choices: Stone castles built for medieval knights

questions.question: What is one reason historians study artifacts from early societies?
choices: Artifacts provide evidence about technology, trade, and daily life
Artifacts always identify their original owners

questions.question: Why did written records matter to some early states?
choices: They ended the need for communication
They guaranteed that every person could read
They helped record transactions, laws, taxes, or administration

questions.question: A river floods unpredictably, damaging fields. Which response could help a community reduce risk?
choices: Build and maintain systems for managing water and storing food
Move every settlement into a desert
Plant crops only after floods occur

questions.question: What is a civilization's social hierarchy?
choices: An arrangement of groups with different status, roles, or access to power
A tool for measuring crop yields
A system that gives everyone identical authority

questions.question: Which material was commonly used in Mesopotamia to make durable writing tablets?
Why might control of a river valley become a source of political power?
choices: It guarantees that no neighboring group can trade
It removes the need for organized labor
It can provide access to water, farmland, and transportation routes

questions.question: Which statement best describes the role of trade in early civilizations?
choices: Trade moved resources and ideas between communities

questions.question: A historian finds evidence that an early town used standardized weights. What might this indicate?
choices: The town had no market activity
People measured goods in ways that could support exchange and administration
Residents used a modern metric system
Weights were used only for building temples

questions.question: Which early Chinese dynasty is associated with oracle bones and bronze work?
Why did some early governments organize labor for canals, walls, or temples?
choices: Every project could be completed by one household
Canals did not require planning or maintenance
Large projects required coordination of workers and resources

questions.question: What is a limitation of using only written records to study early civilizations?
choices: Records may reflect the views of literate elites and omit many people's experiences
Written records always describe every group equally
